prompt:
Scene:
A tight symmetric close-up of a gothic rose window opening, framed by tracery stone and lit from behind. The shot is almost flat-on but with a faint downward tilt that shows the thickness of the stone tracery. Deep indigo stone, cyan projection glow, micro volumetric haze.

Subject:
Where the stained glass would normally sit, there is instead a layered volumetric hologram: concentric geometric rings, rotating slowly in different directions, each ring made of crisp light particles. The hologram is not flat — it has visible depth through the window aperture, with inner rings receding into the wall and outer rings protruding forward. Small motes of light drift around the rim.

Important details:
The stone tracery must look weathered, with chisel marks and slight erosion at the edges. The hologram must feel physically volumetric: particles cluster more densely toward the center, and the rings cast faint concentric light onto the tracery stone. Color is locked to cool cyan with a single warm amber accent at the very center point. Symmetry is strict — the window is radially perfect.

Use case:
Hologram Cathedral Nave single study 1/5, focusing on the volumetric rose window as a standalone subject.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no pictorial saints inside the rose, no crucifix shape, no lens starbursts, no human figures, no banners or cords hanging across the window.
title: Volumetric Rose Window
description: A close-up study of a gothic rose window replaced by a layered volumetric hologram of rotating concentric geometric rings.
